text:
Predicates:
ListedInYelp(x) ::: x is listed in Yelp’s recommendations.
ReceivesManyNegativeReviews(x) ::: x receives many negative reviews.
RatingGreaterThan9(x) ::: x has a rating greater than 9.
ProvidesTakeOut(x) ::: x provides take-out service.
PopularAmongLocals(x) ::: x is popular among local residents.
Subway ::: Subway (the restaurant).

Premises:
∀x (ListedInYelp(x) → ¬ReceivesManyNegativeReviews(x)) ::: If the restaurant is listed in Yelp’s recommendations, then it does not receive many negative reviews.
∀x (Rating(x) > 9 → ListedInYelp(x)) ::: All restaurants with a rating greater than 9 are listed in Yelp’s recommendations.
∃x (¬ProvidesTakeOut(x) ∧ ReceivesManyNegativeReviews(x)) ::: Some restaurants that do not provide take-out service receive many negative reviews.
∀x (PopularAmongLocals(x) → Rating(x) > 9) ::: All restaurants that are popular among local residents have ratings greater than 9.
Rating(Subway) > 9 ∨ PopularAmongLocals(Subway) ::: Subway has a rating greater than 9 or is popular among local residents.

Conclusion:
(ProvidesTakeOut(Subway) ∧ ReceivesManyNegativeReviews(Subway)) → (Rating(Subway) > 9 ∧ ¬ProvidesTakeOut(Subway))
